I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` review workflow to calibrate the merge gate consistently. I’ll treat severity as the primary signal and `scores.agent_risk` as the tie-breaker, while calling out the unusually high-severity/low-agent-risk cases.

The repository-local skill path isn’t present in this fixture checkout, so I’ll use the scan’s supplied JSON directly and preserve its contract fields. No additional scan is needed because your prompt already includes the complete 42-finding output.

I’d gate this PR as **5 block / 32 warn / 5 ignore**.

Because this is an empty baseline, every finding is newly introduced. I use severity as the primary signal and `scores.agent_risk` as prioritization—not as a hard threshold. Agent-risk scores are compressed here because churn and blast-radius inputs are all zero.

### Block merge

| ID | Finding | Severity | Agent risk | Justification |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| crime_00001 | Direct clock reads in `src/date.ts` | high | 0.44 | Highest agent risk in the scan; a clock read controls branching, making domain behavior nondeterministic. |
| crime_00009 | Mixed UTC/local date methods | high | 0.36 | Silent timezone-dependent behavior is a correctness risk and likely to vary between developer, CI, and production hosts. |
| crime_00015 | 204-line `generateInvoice` | high | 0.30 | A 3.4× oversized domain function is too risky to introduce wholesale; interactions are difficult to review and test safely. |
| crime_00032 | Conflicting `User` contracts | high | 0.22 | The lower agent-risk score reflects zero measured churn/blast radius, but the high-severity timestamp disagreement is a real contract-integrity problem. |
| crime_00033 | Conflicting `Invoice` contracts | high | 0.22 | Six critical disagreements—including identity, money, and timestamp fields—make this merge-blocking despite the low contextual risk score. |

### Warn

| ID | Finding | Severity | Agent risk | Justification |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| crime_00002 | Return-shape roulette | low | 0.43 | Low severity, but very high agent risk: three substantially different implicit result shapes invite caller mistakes. |
| crime_00003 | Missing agent context | medium | 0.42 | High-priority warning for a CLI repository; agents cannot discover commands or safety conventions. |
| crime_00004 | Scattered `"enterprise"` policy literal | medium | 0.42 | Four copies across separate areas create a strong duplicated-policy risk. |
| crime_00005 | Duplicated navigation source | medium | 0.38 | Competing labels make partial updates likely. |
| crime_00006 | Route metadata drift | medium | 0.38 | Four competing names for one destination indicate visible product inconsistency. |
| crime_00007 | Synchronous I/O in domain function | low | 0.38 | Low severity, but elevated agent risk and three event-loop-blocking calls warrant follow-up. |
| crime_00008 | Implicit option bag | low | 0.38 | Six undocumented properties make the calling contract difficult to infer safely. |
| crime_00010 | Negative flag maze | low | 0.36 | The combined negations have meaningful inversion risk despite low severity. |
| crime_00011 | Timezone-unsafe parsing | medium | 0.35 | Ambiguous date strings can produce environment-dependent results. |
| crime_00012 | Direct clock reads in billing | medium | 0.34 | These affect output rather than branches, so warn rather than block. |
| crime_00013 | Misleading refund-preview name | medium | 0.31 | A supposedly pure preview sends email and writes audit data; callers may invoke it unsafely. |
| crime_00014 | Authorization rule only in a comment | medium | 0.31 | The owner/support exception appears unenforced and should be encoded or tested. |
| crime_00016 | Hardcoded localhost URL | medium | 0.30 | Newly introduced code will fail outside one development environment. |
| crime_00017 | Hardcoded user path | medium | 0.30 | The path is non-portable across developers, CI, and deployment. |
| crime_00018 | DST-naive day arithmetic | medium | 0.30 | Calendar behavior can silently shift on DST boundaries. |
| crime_00019 | Tenant vocabulary drift | medium | 0.30 | Four aliases across routes and docs create conceptual duplication. |
| crime_00020 | Extreme TODO density | medium | 0.30 | Fourteen markers in 32 lines make intended behavior unclear. |
| crime_00021 | Commented-out implementation | medium | 0.29 | Stale executable-looking code is likely to be copied or revived accidentally. |
| crime_00023 | Direct clock read in state logic | low | 0.28 | It controls a comparison, so deterministic clock handling is advisable. |
| crime_00024 | Singular/plural type mismatch | low | 0.28 | Names directly contradict scalar/array types and can mislead callers. |
| crime_00025 | Test with no assertions | medium | 0.27 | Gives false confidence while protecting no observable behavior. |
| crime_00026 | Manual date-string construction | low | 0.26 | Risks zero-indexed months, padding, and timezone errors. |
| crime_00027 | Host-dependent locale formatting | low | 0.26 | Output varies across runtime environments. |
| crime_00029 | Raster data embedded in SVG | high | 0.24 | High detector severity, but relatively low agent risk and primarily an asset-quality issue; require follow-up rather than blocking the whole PR. |
| crime_00030 | Broken documentation link | low | 0.24 | Concrete stale documentation should be corrected, though it is not merge-critical. |
| crime_00031 | Weak invoice assertion | low | 0.23 | Some assertion exists, but the test may not protect meaningful behavior. |
| crime_00034 | Orphaned account route | low | 0.22 | Confirm whether the route is intentionally in flight, then link or remove it. |
| crime_00035 | Orphaned team route | low | 0.22 | Same reachability concern; intent needs confirmation. |
| crime_00036 | Orphaned workspace route | low | 0.22 | Same reachability concern; intent needs confirmation. |
| crime_00037 | 310-line billing file | medium | 0.18 | Only slightly over the threshold and overlaps with the blocked large function, so it should inform the same refactor rather than independently block. |
| crime_00040 | Swallowed email error | low | 0.12 | The score is low, but silently reporting success after failure is a concrete correctness/observability concern. |
| crime_00041 | Undeclared `vitest` dependency | low | 0.12 | Test-only and low-risk, but a clean install or test run can fail. |

### Ignore for merge purposes

| ID | Finding | Severity | Agent risk | Justification |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| crime_00022 | Boolean naming in `state.ts` | low | 0.29 | Naming consistency only; `paid`, `expired`, and `stale` remain understandable and can be configured as project idioms. |
| crime_00028 | Boolean naming in `petty.ts` | low | 0.26 | The names already communicate negative behavior; renaming would be cosmetic and potentially churn-heavy. |
| crime_00038 | 32×32 raster icon | low | 0.16 | Minor asset-format optimization with no demonstrated functional impact. |
| crime_00039 | 254 KB hero raster | low | 0.14 | Only modestly over the lowest size threshold; optimize later under a defined performance budget. |
| crime_00042 | Four TODO markers in billing | low | 0.08 | Lowest-risk finding and barely above the density threshold; track as cleanup rather than merge work. |

The key review distinction is that `crime_00029` is the sole high-severity finding I would not block on: its impact is asset quality, its agent risk is only `0.24`, and the evidence reports a very small 592-byte file. Conversely, the two contract-drift findings remain blockers despite `0.22` agent risk because their evidence identifies critical domain-field disagreements.
